newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Croatia says won't be pushed to ally with ex-foes.
newsitem.headline: Croatia says won't be pushed to ally with ex-foes.

text.p: Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa said on Friday his country would not be pushed into renewing alliances with other former members of the Yugoslav federation that broke up in 1991.

"In spite of the multiple evidence of the impossibility of a joint state in the area of the former Yugoslavia in the course of the 20th Century, some agents of European policies are making repeated attempts to create some artificial associations and assigning Croatia a place in it beforehand," Matesa said in a speech delivered at a central European summit in Austria.
"Croatia rejects any attempt to make it a party to some artificial political associations," he said.

Croatia has repeatedly said it will not accept what it sees as European Union pressure for the former Yugoslav republics to boost economic cooperation, relax border controls and establish some form of a common market among themselves.
Matesa was attending a two-day summit meeting of the Central European Initiative, a group formed in 1989 to promote regional cooperation and security.
